recommendations.regimenLabel: Immediate high-dose glucocorticoids (IV if visual loss)
steps: START high-dose oral glucocorticoids IMMEDIATELY on suspicion - do not wait for biopsy (sight-threatening); IV methylprednisolone if visual loss.
Prednisone ~40-80 mg/day (Harrison cites 80 mg daily for the first 4-6 weeks).
Arrange temporal artery biopsy (or Doppler US) as soon as practical - steroids do not abolish findings immediately but can mask them with prolonged treatment.
Gastroprotection, bone protection, glucose monitoring; tocilizumab as a steroid-sparing alternative.
Slow steroid taper guided by symptoms and ESR/CRP.

drugRefs.dose: 40–60 mg once daily (Harrison cites up to 80 mg for the first 4–6 weeks), then slow taper
drugRefs.freq: once daily, tapered guided by symptoms and ESR/CRP
drugRefs.why: Start immediately on clinical suspicion to prevent irreversible visual loss; do not wait for biopsy.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: IV pulse corticosteroid (visual loss / impending visual loss)
drugRefs.dose: 500–1000 mg once daily for 3 days, then switch to oral prednisolone
drugRefs.why: For established or impending visual loss; more rapid, high-intensity suppression before stepping down to oral steroid.

drugRefs.why: Bone protection given the prolonged high-dose glucocorticoid course typical of GCA.
